1.name: Brian Bell
1.about: Brian Bell maintained his status as the class's premier prospect throughout an otherwise underwhelming draft cycle. The Memphis freshman showcased explosive finishing, disruptive perimeter defense, and exceptional athleticism. While his inconsistent jumper remains a concern, his two-way versatility and physical upside kept him firmly ahead of the competition.

2.name: Daniel Fernández
2.about: A projected No. 2 overall pick, Fernández has established himself as one of the draft's most exciting international talents. The 6'8" Spanish wing impressed with Baskonia through explosive finishing, fluid perimeter scoring and defensive versatility, showcasing the athleticism and offensive upside of a potential NBA star.

4.name: Arkell Williams
4.about: Extraordinary length made Arkell Williams one of Duke's most intriguing freshmen, disrupting shots and finishing around the basket. His defensive timing, fluid movement, and developing perimeter skills offer tremendous upside. Adding strength, improving his shooting consistency, and refining his offensive game remain essential to his development.

6.name: Vukadin Gavrilović
6.about: Relentless rebounding and impressive passing instincts defined Vukadin Gavrilović's physical freshman campaign at Duke. The Serbian big excelled facilitating from the post and creating second-chance opportunities, while his developing perimeter touch adds intrigue. Defensive mobility and inconsistent shooting remain areas for improvement at the next level.

7.name: Bayley Banks
7.about: Michigan's freshman standout delivered an impressive debut campaign, establishing himself as one of the nation's most polished young scoring guards. Banks thrives attacking the paint, creating separation in the midrange and finishing through contact. His sturdy frame and offensive versatility have strengthened his NBA outlook.

8.name: Derek Allard-Jones
8.about: Kentucky found an immediate interior presence in Derek Allard-Jones, whose explosive athleticism fueled offensive rebounding and intimidating rim protection. The Canadian freshman consistently generated second-chance opportunities while anchoring defensive possessions with his exceptional wingspan. His offensive limitations remain evident, particularly his inconsistent jumper and lack of polished scoring moves.

9.name: Zayden Smith IV
9.about: An explosive sophomore campaign at Marquette elevated Smith's reputation as one of college basketball's most dynamic athletic wings. His aggressive downhill attacks, impressive vertical explosiveness and disruptive defensive instincts consistently impacted games. With improved offensive confidence, Smith has developed into an intriguing two-way NBA prospect.

11.name: Josh Simmons
11.about: A productive sophomore season at Texas Tech showcased Simmons' impressive combination of midrange scoring and defensive instincts. The 6'6" left-hander uses his lengthy frame to disrupt passing lanes while creating offense with polished footwork and controlled shot-making, establishing himself as a promising two-way backcourt prospect.

12.name: Beau Mitchell
12.about: With Melbourne United, Beau Mitchell displayed a compelling mix of perimeter shooting, defensive versatility, and positional size. The Australian forward demonstrated reliable floor-spacing instincts while using his length to contest shots and contribute on the glass. Continued improvements in physicality, offensive creation, and consistency could elevate his long-term NBA potential.

13.name: Jake Collins
13.about: A versatile freshman at USC, Jake Collins offers an intriguing blend of interior finishing, perimeter shooting, and defensive potential. His 7'3" wingspan gives him the tools to contest shots around the basket, while his ability to stretch the floor creates additional space for teammates. Collins can play either frontcourt position, contribute as a lob target, and develop into a modern two-way big whose combination of size and shooting provides long-term NBA upside.
13.pro_comp: Jusuf Nurkić with a Jump Shot

14.name: Dane Burger
14.about: With his combination of size and elite perimeter touch, Dane Burger offers an intriguing stretch-big profile after his sophomore season at Boston College. The 7'1" center can pull opposing bigs away from the basket with his 81-rated three-point shooting, opening driving lanes for teammates. His length also gives him tools to challenge shots inside and contribute on the glass. Burger's shooting versatility and interior presence create a promising foundation for a modern frontcourt role.

15.name: Adam Ortega
15.about: A polished offensive connector, Adam Ortega capped his Iowa career with an impressive senior campaign built around efficient perimeter shooting and advanced passing instincts. His size, floor spacing, and quick decision-making make him particularly effective in structured offenses, although limited athleticism and defensive mobility create concerns against quicker NBA wings.

16.name: Aaron Azoulay
16.about: Playing professionally in France, Azoulay demonstrated encouraging development as a versatile young combo guard for SIG Strasbourg. His impressive wingspan, controlled ball handling and developing playmaking instincts allowed him to contribute in multiple backcourt roles. His composure and basketball intelligence provide a promising foundation for NBA development.

18.name: Jumaane Jakande
18.about: Nigerian freshman Jumaane Jakande brings a powerful interior game to Oklahoma, combining a sturdy 263-pound frame with a 7'6" wingspan and explosive finishing ability. He thrives on forceful dunks, strong rolls to the basket, and physical play around the rim. His length gives him promising defensive potential, while his strength helps him establish position and battle for rebounds. Jakande has the tools to develop into an imposing paint presence with a clear identity as a high-energy finisher.

19.name: Noah Jakobsson
19.about: Noah Jakobsson finished his UConn career as a dependable offensive facilitator, combining smooth perimeter shooting with impressive passing instincts. The Swedish forward excelled at keeping possessions flowing and exploiting defensive rotations, offering valuable versatility in half-court sets. Average athleticism and limited defensive range remain concerns against quicker opponents.

21.name: Darryon Jenkins
21.about: VCU's defensive identity benefited tremendously from Jenkins, whose junior campaign highlighted his value as a dependable two-way contributor. The 6'4" guard combined accurate perimeter shooting with disruptive on-ball defense, using his exceptional wingspan to challenge opposing scorers. His complementary skill set translates naturally to an NBA role.

22.name: Dmitry Yaroslavsky
22.about: Texas found a valuable perimeter weapon in Yaroslavsky, whose freshman campaign showcased advanced shooting instincts and impressive offensive finesse. The 6'7" Russian wing consistently created separation with crafty footwork, smooth shooting mechanics and intelligent off-ball movement, establishing himself as an intriguing offensive prospect with NBA potential.

23.name: Omontae Miller
23.about: Few freshmen matched Omontae Miller's physical presence around the basket, as the Baylor forward consistently delivered thunderous finishes and intimidating defensive plays. His exceptional length, explosive leaping, and ability to erase shots highlight considerable two-way upside. However, an inconsistent jumper and developing offensive fundamentals limit his immediate versatility.

24.name: Darrell Murphy
24.about: Once considered a top-10 prospect entering the season, Murphy saw his draft stock decline despite showcasing impressive perimeter scoring at Oklahoma. The physical freshman guard displayed deep shooting range, confident shot creation and a quick release, but an inconsistent debut campaign ultimately tempered his early expectations.

26.name: Jan Ebner
26.about: Efficient perimeter shooting and disciplined interior defense made Florida junior Jan Ebner a dependable two-way contributor. The German junior stretched opposing defenses with his spot-up shooting while providing timely shot contests around the basket. Limited mobility and difficulty creating offense independently remain concerns about his NBA transition.

27.name: Tyler Dean
27.about: Tyler Dean emerged as Colorado State's primary offensive catalyst, blending aggressive downhill drives with impressive playmaking instincts. His ability to collapse defenses and locate open teammates fueled a productive junior campaign. While his positional versatility and passing stand out, inconsistent perimeter shooting and limited explosiveness complicate his offensive projection.

29.name: Luke Bannerman
29.about: Australian frontcourt prospect Luke Bannerman brings energy and athleticism to Stanford, using his 6'11" frame and 7'3" wingspan to create opportunities around the basket. He excels at cutting into open space, running the floor, and finishing through contact, making him a natural target in transition and pick-and-roll actions. His mobility and physical tools provide a foundation for growth as an energetic two-way big who can impact possessions without needing the ball in his hands.

33.name: Latrelle Hayes
33.about: A high-energy freshman at UCLA, Latrelle Hayes brings a powerful frame and impressive length to the frontcourt despite standing 6'8". His 7'3" wingspan helps him finish above defenders, attack the offensive glass, and disrupt plays around the basket. Hayes thrives when cutting into open space, running the floor, and using his strength around the rim. With his physical tools and willingness to play an active off-ball role, he has an appealing foundation as an energetic interior contributor.

34.name: Samba Sow
34.about: In Senegal, Samba Sow drew attention through energetic interior play, an impressive wingspan, and disruptive defensive instincts. The athletic forward consistently challenged shots near the rim while finishing effectively off cuts and offensive rebounds. His limited shooting and developing fundamentals remain obstacles to NBA readiness.

35.name: Daniel Cleveland
35.about: After transferring from USC to Gonzaga, Cleveland made the most of his final collegiate season, emerging as a dependable offensive contributor. The 6'6" senior showcased polished midrange scoring, physical downhill attacks and controlled footwork, using his experience to strengthen his appeal as an NBA rotational prospect.

36.name: Matthew Osborne
36.about: Matthew Osborne brings a polished shooting touch and a crafty offensive approach to Texas's frontcourt. The 6'11" junior can stretch the defense with his 77-rated three-point shot, giving teammates more room to attack and creating mismatches against traditional centers. He uses patience and touch to score around the basket, while his size allows him to compete on the glass and contribute as a versatile frontcourt option. Osborne's shooting gives him a clear path toward a specialized professional role.

37.name: Éloi Pommier
37.about: A mobile French big with an exciting two-way toolkit, Éloi Pommier combines above-the-rim finishing with the length to make a difference defensively. His 7'3" wingspan helps him challenge shots, while his athleticism makes him a dangerous lob target and an effective runner in transition. With a developing perimeter shot that can help pull opposing centers away from the basket, Pommier has the foundation to become a versatile frontcourt contributor who impacts both ends.
37.pro_comp: Nic Claxton with a Jump Shot

38.name: Shawn Anderson
38.about: A former four-star recruit, Shawn Anderson spent three seasons at Washington before transferring to Duke for his senior year. The lengthy forward established himself as a versatile defensive specialist, disrupting passing lanes and protecting the rim. However, inconsistent perimeter shooting and limited offensive creation continue to restrict his ceiling.

39.name: Kam Turner
39.about: Kam Turner took a meaningful step forward during his sophomore season at Xavier, developing into a productive slashing wing with improved perimeter confidence. His length, fluid athleticism, and ability to finish above the rim create intriguing offensive opportunities. However, inconsistent decision-making and limited shot creation remain areas requiring refinement.

40.name: Justyn Simmons
40.about: A steady presence in Wake Forest's backcourt, Simmons capped his junior campaign with an impressive display of offensive creativity and basketball intelligence. The 6'5" combo guard relied on crafty ball handling, patient pick-and-roll execution and difficult fadeaway jumpers to create scoring opportunities while orchestrating the offense.

41.name: Dazhawn Williams
41.about: Dazhawn Williams flashed intriguing shot-making ability throughout his freshman campaign at Washington, displaying a smooth pull-up jumper and confidence operating from the midrange. His size and shooting touch provide a promising offensive foundation, but inconsistent efficiency, limited explosiveness, and defensive lapses prevented him from establishing a more complete game.

42.name: Gela Andronikashvili
42.about: Gela Andronikashvili brings a patient, touch-oriented scoring style to the frontcourt, using his size and left-handed finishing to work effectively around the paint. He shows promise as a short-range shot-maker who can score with soft hooks, floaters, and controlled finishes over defenders. His 259-pound frame gives him a sturdy base for interior play, while his developing offensive feel creates opportunities to become a dependable scoring option around the basket and midrange.

45.name: Ryan Adams
45.about: A reliable floor-spacing presence throughout his Creighton career, Ryan Adams paired consistent perimeter shooting with intelligent defensive positioning. The senior excelled in pick-and-pop situations and provided timely rim protection despite modest athletic tools. His limited lateral mobility and struggles creating offense could restrict his versatility against NBA competition.

47.name: Matt McGraw
47.about: Matt McGraw offers a skilled offensive profile built around his size, shooting touch, and ability to create space for teammates. At 6'11", he can pull opposing bigs away from the paint with his 78-rated three-point shot, making him a useful pick-and-pop option. His patient approach and soft touch give him additional scoring options inside, while his experience as a senior helps him bring composure and structure to the frontcourt. McGraw projects as a floor-spacing big who can complement more athletic players.

48.name: Kash Smith
48.about: A former five-star recruit, Kash Smith arrived at Houston with considerable expectations but endured an inconsistent freshman campaign. His explosive athleticism, defensive length, and transition finishing provided flashes of his highly regarded talent. However, limited offensive polish, a slender frame, and unreliable perimeter shooting contributed to an underwhelming debut season.

50.name: A.J. Mdogo
50.about: A.J. Mdogo brings exciting length and athleticism to Tennessee's frontcourt, with a 7'5" wingspan that helps him finish above the rim and disrupt shots around the basket. His quickness and vertical pop make him a natural lob target who can sprint the floor, attack open lanes, and thrive as a roll man in pick-and-roll actions. At 230 pounds, he has room to add strength while developing his defensive instincts and offensive range. Mdogo's physical tools give him an intriguing foundation as an energetic two-way center.

51.name: Somondre Williams
51.about: Physicality defined Somondre Williams' junior campaign at UCLA, where he established himself as a rugged interior scorer and dependable rebounder. His strong frame, effective screening, and willingness to battle through contact provided valuable frontcourt contributions. However, limited vertical explosiveness and inconsistent perimeter shooting restrict his versatility against athletic defenders.

52.name: Brandon Hurst
52.about: Physical rebounding and dependable perimeter shooting became the hallmarks of Brandon Hurst's final season at Nebraska. The senior consistently battled for positioning, created second-chance opportunities, and stretched defenses from beyond the arc. However, limited mobility, below-the-rim finishing, and defensive shortcomings raise concerns about his NBA fit.

53.name: Jacoby David
53.about: Relentless energy and physicality powered Jacoby David's work in Florida State's frontcourt, especially on rebounds and interior finishes. His exceptional wingspan helped compensate for his undersized frame, particularly when battling for offensive boards. However, limited shooting range, inconsistent defensive positioning, and raw offensive skills restrict his versatility.

54.name: Javari Stevens
54.about: Javari Stevens closed his Houston career as a physical two-way contributor, combining aggressive interior scoring with dependable perimeter defense. His strength, long wingspan, and willingness to attack mismatches made him effective in multiple roles. However, inconsistent outside shooting and limited offensive creativity restrict his ability to generate reliable scoring opportunities.

55.name: Matthew Drake
55.about: Matthew Drake finished his Clemson career as a reliable perimeter scoring option, using his size and left-handed shooting touch to stretch defenses. His ability to find openings off the ball and convert contested jumpers provided consistent offense, although limited athleticism and defensive mobility raise concerns about his professional transition.

56.name: Myles Dupree
56.about: Defensive assignments became Myles Dupree's calling card at Illinois, where athleticism, physicality, and effort frustrated opposing forwards. The sophomore excelled switching onto perimeter players and disrupting passing lanes, but his offensive contributions remained limited. Poor outside shooting and inconsistent scoring instincts significantly restrict his NBA upside.

57.name: Vedran Gojak
57.about: Gojak flashed intriguing offensive potential during his season with SC Derby, using his 6'7" frame to attack the basket and finish above the rim. The Croatian wing demonstrated encouraging transition scoring instincts and developing defensive versatility, although his limited offensive polish leaves him a developmental NBA prospect.

58.name: Maalik Bates
58.about: Maalik Bates concluded his UTSA career as an energetic, athletic forward who thrived attacking the rim and finishing in transition. His impressive leaping ability, strong frame, and rebounding activity created consistent opportunities around the basket. However, inconsistent perimeter shooting and limited offensive versatility raise questions about his professional scoring role.

59.name: Jack Owens
59.about: Jack Owens carved out a dependable scoring role at Wisconsin, relying on polished shooting mechanics and intelligent off-ball movement throughout his junior campaign. His perimeter accuracy and disciplined shot selection made him a valuable floor spacer, but poor athleticism and defensive limitations significantly narrow his potential professional contributions.

61.name: Trenten McMullen
61.about: Impressive passing vision and dependable perimeter touch helped Trenten McMullen serve as Michigan's skilled offensive connector. The senior facilitated effectively from the high post, kept possessions flowing, and stretched defenses with timely outside shooting. However, limited athleticism and defensive mobility complicate his prospects at the professional level.

62.name: Myles Sosa
62.about: Davidson's veteran sharpshooter closed his collegiate career with an impressive display of perimeter scoring, consistently stretching defenses with his deep shooting range. Sosa excelled navigating screens, relocating off the ball and converting difficult jumpers, but his limited physical tools leave him fighting for an NBA opportunity.

63.name: Dannell Christian
63.about: In transition, Dannell Christian gave Jacksonville State an energetic scoring threat through his physical frame and open-court instincts. The senior excelled pushing the pace, finishing through contact, and contributing on the glass. His inconsistent perimeter shooting and limited half-court creation leave questions about his professional outlook.

64.name: Mircea Bologa
64.about: At ALBA Berlin, Mircea Bologa flashed offensive versatility through interior finishing and developing perimeter touch. The Romanian forward found opportunities as a cutter and pick-and-pop option, but struggled to establish consistent production against experienced competition. Limited athleticism, defensive mobility, and an unreliable jumper cloud his NBA outlook.

65.name: Max Hannah
65.about: Timely cuts, opportunistic finishing, and relentless off-ball movement made Max Hannah an energetic presence for Wyoming. The junior demonstrated solid rebounding instincts and occasional perimeter touch, but his undersized frame and limited shot creation make projecting a consistent NBA role increasingly difficult at the next level.

66.name: Treyvon Williams
66.about: Arkansas benefited from Williams' relentless energy throughout his senior campaign, particularly on the defensive end and in transition. Despite standing 6'4", his exceptional wingspan and explosive leaping ability allowed him to challenge bigger opponents, finish spectacularly above the rim and generate several momentum-changing defensive plays.

67.name: Malick Kouyaté
67.about: Standing an imposing 7'4" with a remarkable 7'9" wingspan, Malick Kouyaté offers rare size and reach at the center position. He can change shots simply by occupying space near the rim, challenge finishes at the basket, and provide a massive target for lob passes and interior feeds. His 280-pound frame gives him a strong physical base for battling inside, while his enormous reach creates opportunities to collect rebounds and finish over defenders. Kouyaté has a distinctive foundation as a paint-focused center whose size can shape both ends of the floor.

68.name: Vitalii Rudyk
68.about: Vitalii Rudyk brings a crafty scoring touch and a versatile offensive skill set to the frontcourt. At 6'9", he can operate as a small-ball center or power forward, using his left hand and comfortable shooting stroke to score from the midrange and stretch the floor. His 70-rated three-point shot gives him value as a pick-and-pop option, while his ability to create soft-touch finishes around the paint adds another dimension to his game. Rudyk's offensive versatility gives him an intriguing role as a skilled frontcourt scorer.

69.name: Brandon Kelley
69.about: Brandon Kelley combines exceptional length with a developing face-up scoring game, giving Gonzaga a versatile interior presence. At 7'1" with a 7'7" wingspan, he has the reach to contest shots, collect rebounds, and finish over defenders. His midrange touch adds another scoring dimension, allowing him to operate from the elbows and attack closeouts. With his size and defensive potential, Kelley has the foundation to grow into a rim-protecting big who can also contribute offensively without needing constant touches.

70.name: Aaron Jimenez
70.about: Closing his collegiate career at Cal Poly, Jimenez showcased intriguing physical tools and flashes of offensive versatility. The 6'8" senior utilized his length to finish above the rim, attack open lanes and contribute defensively. His combination of positional size and slashing instincts offers developmental appeal.

71.name: Ben Mullin
71.about: Physical finishing, disciplined defense, and steady rebounding defined Ben Mullin's final season at Gonzaga. The senior understood his role, capitalizing on opportunities around the basket while competing defensively. Limited athleticism, inconsistent perimeter shooting, and modest offensive versatility make an NBA opportunity unlikely at the next level.

72.name: Kaenan Wilkerson
72.about: Kaenan Wilkerson displayed occasional scoring flashes during his junior season at Texas Tech, relying on difficult pull-up jumpers and creative perimeter footwork. His length and shot-making confidence provide some offensive intrigue, but inconsistent efficiency, limited physicality, and defensive shortcomings leave him facing an uncertain path toward a professional opportunity.

73.name: Justin Boone
73.about: A transfer from Marshall, Justin Boone supplied Texas with bruising interior play, physical rebounding, powerful putbacks, and relentless effort. The undersized senior competed against larger opponents but offered little offensive versatility. Severe shooting limitations and inconsistent defensive mobility make an NBA selection unlikely at the next level.
